Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details

- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Dr Smith, Practice: Babylon (digital service), Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Work-related anxiety disorder / possible Generalized Anxiety Disorder (provisional)
- Secondary: Insomnia secondary to anxiety
- Tertiary: Palpitations likely anxiety-related; rule out medical causes

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: None currently (no regular medications documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: None recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): None recorded
- Family History: Mother with past depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with both parents
- Social Support: Describes “good support system” from family
- Occupation/Education: New job (2 months) in fashion-retail head-office; high stress; unsupportive manager
- Alcohol Use: Heavy binge drinking most Fridays/Saturdays (quantities not stated); occasional mid-week wine; exact units unknown
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasional smoking; denies illicit drug use
- Key Stressors: New stressful job, critical boss, fear of lateness, crowded public transport (tube), chronic worry

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Appears distressed/anxious; cooperative; appropriate eye contact (inferred from video call)
- Mood & Affect: Subjective mood “really anxious” and “down”; affect anxious, congruent
- Speech & Thought: Normal rate/volume; thought content preoccupied with work stress; no thought-form abnormalities
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Alert and oriented (time, person, situation)
- Attention/Concentration: Likely reduced due to anxiety (not formally tested)
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Good insight; appropriately seeks help

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: 3-4 hrs/night; prolonged sleep-onset; early awakening with palpitations
- Appetite: Largely unchanged; mild increase in chocolate intake
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly reduced daytime energy and enjoyment
- Anxiety Symptoms: Persistent worry, dread, racing/irregular heartbeat, physical tension, avoidance of social/fitness activities

Risk Assessment
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or thoughts of harming others
- Protective Factors: Supportive family, intact insight, employment, willingness to engage in therapy
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation
Predisposing: Family history of depression; personal high standards.  
Precipitating: Onset of demanding new job with critical supervisor two months ago.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing workplace stress, anticipatory worry, poor sleep, occasional binge alcohol use, avoidance of enjoyable activities/exercise.  
Protective: Supportive parents, insight, motivation to seek help.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related anxiety / possible GAD
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Feel calmer at work and before leaving home  
  • Regain enjoyment in daily activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Reduce anxiety symptom severity (worry, palpitations)  
  • Improve functional capacity at work and socially
- Actions (Patient):
  • Self-refer to NHS talking-therapy (IAPT/CBT) via link provided  
  • Begin recommended online CBT resources immediately  
  • Practice daily relaxation/breathing exercises; limit caffeine/alcohol  
  • Monitor anxiety triggers and severity; seek review if deterioration
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide self-referral link and online CBT resources via patient portal  
  • Provide written information on anxiety management and relaxation techniques  
  • Review progress and consider pharmacotherapy if symptoms persist or worsen

Secondary Problem: Insomnia
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Achieve 7–8 hours restful sleep
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Reduce sleep-onset latency; normalize sleep pattern
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement sleep-hygiene strategies (consistent bedtime, screen curfew, wind-down routine)  
  • Reduce late-evening alcohol intake  
  • Reintroduce light exercise (e.g., running, tennis) earlier in day
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide written sleep-hygiene guidance  
  • Review sleep quality at follow-up; consider further interventions if needed

Tertiary Problem: Palpitations
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Decrease frequency/intensity of palpitations
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Exclude organic causes; reassure patient; link to anxiety management
- Actions (Patient):
  • Attend ordered blood tests; record occurrence/time/duration of palpitations
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Order basic blood tests (FBC, TFTs, electrolytes, etc.)  
  • Arrange follow-up appointment 1 week post-tests to review results and consider ECG if indicated

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety triggers, CBT/self-help resources, sleep hygiene, importance of routine exercise, limits on alcohol/caffeine
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Inability to attend work, escalating palpitations, panic attacks, marked sleep loss, withdrawal from family/friends
- Coping Strategies: Breathing exercises, scheduled pleasurable activities, graded return to exercise, use of CBT techniques, prompt GP review if symptoms escalate

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded (to be uploaded to patient portal)
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Planned referral to NHS talking-therapy (IAPT/CBT service)
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 4–6 weeks or sooner if deterioration

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Exact alcohol units, medication doses (none taken), objective cognitive testing, emergency contact details  
● Internal conflicts: None noted  
● Transcript quality notes: Single-speaker name occasionally omitted; overall clear audio; no sections on physical examination beyond palpitation description
